new_jobs.title: Tech Infra Program Manager, DC Power Utilization Management
new_jobs.description:
**DESCRIPTION**
---------------


About the Role  

  

Amazon Web Services (AWS) is seeking a Technical Infrastructure Program Manager (TIPM) to join the Power \& Utilization Management and Planning (PUMP) team within AWS Infrastructure Services. This role is responsible for driving programs that maximize power capacity, improve position planning accuracy, and accelerate rack deployment across AWS's global fleet of data centers.  

  

What You'll Do  

  

As a TIPM on the PUMP team, you will own sub\-workstreams within one or more of the following program areas, working under the guidance of senior TIPMs who hold end\-to\-end accountability. You will drive execution on defined scopes, remove blockers, coordinate across partner teams, and progressively take on broader ownership as you build domain expertise.  

  

Data Center Position Configuration \& Automation
  

  

The Soapstone workflow produces three interdependent datasets per build — rack placement on the floor plan, power circuit\-to\-rack mapping (which determines what whips get physically installed), and network cabling plans (which determine how server racks connect to aggregation racks). These outputs determine what gets physically built: general contractors install whips from them, electrical engineers configure three\-phase power equipment at the rack level, and mechanical engineers reference them for downstream work. When this workflow is delayed or incorrect, construction stalls, hardware ships to positions that cannot support it, and capacity delivery slips. You will own sub\-workstreams within this pipeline — for example, driving configuration for a set of availability zones, managing the intake and validation process through SLATE (the team's build coordination portal), or accelerating Hamlet automation coverage to new building classes (COLO sites, hybrid floor plans, Room 1 configurations).  

  

Power Reclamation \& Infrastructure Upgrades
  

  

You will drive specific remediation campaigns that recover stranded power across legacy data centers through electrical upgrades, PDC (Power Distribution Cabinet) deployments, cooling improvements, and breaker\-level optimizations. The power distribution landscape is complex: four distinct PDC versions are active in the fleet with different breaker counts and ampacity ratings, whip counts range from 18 to 26 per rack depending on product type, and whip lengths are tracked manually in Excel files rather than any system of record. You will coordinate across Field Remediation Engineering (FRE), Construction Project Implementation (CPI), Colocation Regional Engineering (CRE), and equipment procurement teams to execute physical infrastructure changes on time.  

  

Network \& Server Position Planning
  

  

You will own sub\-workstreams that improve how network and server positions are planned, allocated, and made ready for deployment. A key challenge is that every rack product connects to the network differently — connection protocols vary (RoCE vs. EFA), server\-to\-switch ratios vary (3:1, 2:1, 1:1\), and switch rack generations keep evolving (12\.8T, 51\.2T, 102\.4T Ultra). You will work with Fulfillment Planning (FP), Capacity Delivery Planning (CDP), and Global Network Deployment (GND) on initiatives like the Fungible Network program, which deploys a standard product\-agnostic network footprint per ROMP so that product flips no longer require cabling rework. You will use and improve tools like RATS and PRP to increase allocation rates and reduce rejection rates at scale.  

  

Power Data Modeling \& Metrics
  

  

You will contribute to the development and maintenance of power\-related data models, dashboards, and sources of truth that inform executive\-level decisions on capacity investment, utilization targets, and demand planning. This includes working with data engineering and BI teams to build QuickSight dashboards, validate Power SOT (Source of Truth) data, and support Monthly and Weekly Business Reviews.  

  

Utility Power Management
  

  

You will support programs that optimize utility power utilization to meet contractual obligations and avoid financial penalties. This includes monitoring site\-level deployed load against contracted capacity, identifying sites at risk of under\-utilization, and coordinating with energy and operations teams to improve utilization rates.  

  

Cross\-Functional Stakeholder Management
  

  

You will work daily with 10\+ partner organizations including CDP, CRE, CPI, FRE, DCEO, GND, Hardware Engineering, ML Planning, AISS Science, and Networking. Success in this role requires the ability to influence without authority, drive accountability across organizational boundaries, and escalate effectively when blockers arise.  

  

About the team  

The PUMP team sits at the intersection of data center engineering, supply chain operations, and capacity planning. We own the end\-to\-end lifecycle of how power is planned, configured, allocated, and utilized across thousands of lineups, hundreds of data centers, and dozens of clusters worldwide. Our decisions directly impact AWS's ability to deliver compute, storage, and machine learning capacity to customers — from core EC2 workloads to the latest GPU\-accelerated ML platforms like GB300, VR200, and TRN3Max.

**BASIC QUALIFICATIONS**
------------------------

* Bachelor's degree in Engineering, Computer Science, or a related technical field
* Experience in project management disciplines including scope, schedule, budget, quality, along with risk and critical path management

new_jobs.description:
**DESCRIPTION**
---------------


About the Role  

  

Amazon Web Services (AWS) is seeking a Technical Infrastructure Program Manager (TIPM) to join the Power \& Utilization Management and Planning (PUMP) team within AWS Infrastructure Services. This role is responsible for driving programs that maximize power capacity, improve position planning accuracy, and accelerate rack deployment across AWS's global fleet of data centers.  

  

What You'll Do  

  

As a TIPM on the PUMP team, you will own sub\-workstreams within one or more of the following program areas, working under the guidance of senior TIPMs who hold end\-to\-end accountability. You will drive execution on defined scopes, remove blockers, coordinate across partner teams, and progressively take on broader ownership as you build domain expertise.  

  

Data Center Position Configuration \& Automation
  

  

The Soapstone workflow produces three interdependent datasets per build — rack placement on the floor plan, power circuit\-to\-rack mapping (which determines what whips get physically installed), and network cabling plans (which determine how server racks connect to aggregation racks). These outputs determine what gets physically built: general contractors install whips from them, electrical engineers configure three\-phase power equipment at the rack level, and mechanical engineers reference them for downstream work. When this workflow is delayed or incorrect, construction stalls, hardware ships to positions that cannot support it, and capacity delivery slips. You will own sub\-workstreams within this pipeline — for example, driving configuration for a set of availability zones, managing the intake and validation process through SLATE (the team's build coordination portal), or accelerating Hamlet automation coverage to new building classes (COLO sites, hybrid floor plans, Room 1 configurations).  

  

Power Reclamation \& Infrastructure Upgrades
  

  

You will drive specific remediation campaigns that recover stranded power across legacy data centers through electrical upgrades, PDC (Power Distribution Cabinet) deployments, cooling improvements, and breaker\-level optimizations. The power distribution landscape is complex: four distinct PDC versions are active in the fleet with different breaker counts and ampacity ratings, whip counts range from 18 to 26 per rack depending on product type, and whip lengths are tracked manually in Excel files rather than any system of record. You will coordinate across Field Remediation Engineering (FRE), Construction Project Implementation (CPI), Colocation Regional Engineering (CRE), and equipment procurement teams to execute physical infrastructure changes on time.  

  

Network \& Server Position Planning
  

  

You will own sub\-workstreams that improve how network and server positions are planned, allocated, and made ready for deployment. A key challenge is that every rack product connects to the network differently — connection protocols vary (RoCE vs. EFA), server\-to\-switch ratios vary (3:1, 2:1, 1:1\), and switch rack generations keep evolving (12\.8T, 51\.2T, 102\.4T Ultra). You will work with Fulfillment Planning (FP), Capacity Delivery Planning (CDP), and Global Network Deployment (GND) on initiatives like the Fungible Network program, which deploys a standard product\-agnostic network footprint per ROMP so that product flips no longer require cabling rework. You will use and improve tools like RATS and PRP to increase allocation rates and reduce rejection rates at scale.  

  

Power Data Modeling \& Metrics
  

  

You will contribute to the development and maintenance of power\-related data models, dashboards, and sources of truth that inform executive\-level decisions on capacity investment, utilization targets, and demand planning. This includes working with data engineering and BI teams to build QuickSight dashboards, validate Power SOT (Source of Truth) data, and support Monthly and Weekly Business Reviews.  

  

Utility Power Management
  

  

You will support programs that optimize utility power utilization to meet contractual obligations and avoid financial penalties. This includes monitoring site\-level deployed load against contracted capacity, identifying sites at risk of under\-utilization, and coordinating with energy and operations teams to improve utilization rates.  

  

Cross\-Functional Stakeholder Management
  

  

You will work daily with 10\+ partner organizations including CDP, CRE, CPI, FRE, DCEO, GND, Hardware Engineering, ML Planning, AISS Science, and Networking. Success in this role requires the ability to influence without authority, drive accountability across organizational boundaries, and escalate effectively when blockers arise.  

  

About the team  

The PUMP team sits at the intersection of data center engineering, supply chain operations, and capacity planning. We own the end\-to\-end lifecycle of how power is planned, configured, allocated, and utilized across thousands of lineups, hundreds of data centers, and dozens of clusters worldwide. Our decisions directly impact AWS's ability to deliver compute, storage, and machine learning capacity to customers — from core EC2 workloads to the latest GPU\-accelerated ML platforms like GB300, VR200, and TRN3Max.

* Experience working with data and leveraging analytics to make decisions

Data Analyst – Job Profile

**Job Title:** Data Analyst  
**Department:** Business Intelligence / Finance / Operations  
**Location:** UAE  
**Reports To:** Finance Manager / Business Head / Management

Job Purpose

The Data Analyst will be responsible for collecting, analysing, interpreting, and presenting business data to support management in making informed decisions. The role will focus on identifying trends, monitoring KPIs, preparing dashboards and reports, and providing actionable insights to improve business performance.

Key Responsibilities

**1\. Data Management**

* Collect data from ERP, accounting, sales, inventory, e\-commerce and other business systems.
* Clean, validate and organize data to ensure accuracy.
* Maintain structured databases, reports and analytical files.
* Identify data inconsistencies and coordinate with relevant departments to resolve them.

**2\. Business \& Sales Analytics**

* Analyse sales by product, brand, customer, channel and region.
* Track sales targets versus actual performance.
* Identify fast\-moving and slow\-moving products.
* Analyse customer purchasing patterns and trends.
* Monitor Amazon, e\-commerce and modern\-trade performance where applicable.

**3\. Inventory \& Supply Chain Analytics**

* Monitor inventory levels and stock movements.
* Analyse stock ageing and slow\-moving inventory.
* Prepare demand and sales forecasts.
* Identify potential stock\-out and overstock situations.
* Analyse purchase, shipment and logistics data.

**4\. Financial Analytics**

* Prepare revenue, gross\-margin and profitability analysis.
* Analyse product\-level profitability.
* Monitor discounts, promotions and commercial support.
* Prepare budget versus actual reports.
* Support management with cost and margin analysis.

**5\. Dashboard \& Reporting**

* Develop daily, weekly and monthly management reports.
* Create interactive dashboards using **Power BI, Tableau or similar tools**.
* Present KPIs and trends in a clear and understandable format.
* Automate repetitive reporting wherever possible.

**6\. Data\-Driven Decision Support**

* Identify trends, opportunities and potential business risks.
* Provide insights rather than simply presenting data.
* Support management in pricing, product selection, inventory planning and sales strategy.
* Develop analytical models to support business decisions.

Required Skills

* Advanced **Microsoft Excel**
* **Power BI** or Tableau
* SQL
* Data visualization
* Business intelligence
* Statistical analysis
* Forecasting and trend analysis
* Strong analytical and problem\-solving skills
* Excellent attention to detail
* Ability to communicate complex data in simple business terms

* Data Analytics
* Business Analytics
* Statistics
* Finance

new_jobs.title: Black Infant Health - Program Manager
new_jobs.description:
#### **POSITION SUMMARY:**


The Black Infant Health (BIH) Program is meant to address the problem of poor birth outcomes and health disparities that affect African American women and their babies. The BIH program features a standard set of services that features group intervention and social service case management to help reduce stress, build resilience, promote healthy behaviors, and increase social support. The BIH Program Manager will have day to day responsibility for leadership of the BIH program and oversee all program team members and partners. This includes developing relationships with community\-based collectives, community\-based organization partners, and management of the Community Advisory Board. The position also includes management of project timelines and deliverables for timely and effective execution of the Work Plan and responsibility for project reporting. Ongoing and timely communication with Alameda County Public Health Department and other community partners will be expected as well. This position supports Alameda County’s BIH Program Area 2, covering families who reside in West Oakland, Emeryville, North Oakland and South Berkeley.


#### **QUALIFICATIONS:**


1\. Education: Bachelor’s Degree from an accredited college or university program in Social Work, Public Health, Nursing, Education, Health Education, or other health related or social science field plus five years of management experience in a health/public health or social service setting is required; or Master’s Degree from an accredited college or university program in Social Work, Public Health, Nursing, Education, Health Education, or other health related or social science field.


2\. Experience: Lived understanding of African American culture and history, and general working knowledge of family systems, community trauma, and community organizing or advocacy. Experience in serving Black birthing and parenting individuals, providing family support, and offering home visiting services is key. At least five years of professional administrative experience in public health or a related field, including two years of supervisory experience.


3\. CA Department of Public Health Approval: The BIH Program Manager must be approved by the California Department of Public Health (CDPH)/Maternal Child and Adolescent Health (MCAH) BIH Program Consultant prior to appointment.


4\. Black Infant Health Ambassador: Fully embraces and supports the Black Infant Health Governing Concepts of culturally relevant, client\-centered, strength\-based, and cognitive skill\-building approaches.


5\. Cultural Competence: Demonstrates cultural competence. Demonstrates ability to implement and maintain a culturally relevant BIH Program that recruits, trains, and retains staff who reflect and respond to the values of the African American community served by BIH.


6\. Knowledge of Public Health: Demonstrates knowledge of the following: women’s health, including prenatal and postpartum health; life course perspective; infant behavior and development; health education, including breastfeeding, nutrition, and physical activity; and local community and social services.


7\. Advocacy and Outreach Skills: Essential qualifications focus on strong community engagement, population\-based assessment, and evidence\-based service delivery skills, particularly in women's health, infant behavior, health education, and addressing health inequities affecting the Black community. Advocacy and outreach skills will be essential to promote health equity by implementing health programs and health policies that will benefit the community’s health through motivational training.


8\. Interpersonal and Leadership Skills: Possess strong leadership skills. Demonstrates the organizational and interpersonal skills needed to communicate at different levels and work in complex situations. Reflects basic skills of the Health Resources and Services Administration Maternal Child Health Bureau Leadership Competencies 1\-8 (leadership.mchtraining.net).


9\. Computer Skills: Basic computer skills, and capable of using software and technology tools used to manage health data and reporting tools (Excel, Microsoft word, etc.). Experience in managing and tracking health data, navigating Epic and Tableau a plus.


10\. Other: Should be able to remain calm and courteous in a high stress environment. Should be able to work independently with minimal direction.

#### **EXAMPLE OF DUTIES:**


1\. Program Management: Responsible for the management and coordination of local BIH program activities and staff. Maintains confidentiality and adheres to Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act (HIPAA) regulations. Provides supervision and professional development for staff; including assignment responsibilities and preparing performance evaluations. Prepares the BIH program budget and monitors expenditures. Prepares administrative, financial documents and transactions for completion, and gathers and compiles information for biannual reports.


2\. Conduct community outreach and need assessments. The BIH program manager will plan, develop, and provide oversight outreach campaigns to enroll pregnant African American women into the Black Infant Health program. Will conduct needs assessments and guide the research, and analysis of statistical and other data to report healthy birth outcomes and effectiveness of the BIH program. Will develop outreach and program literature to raise awareness of African American infant and maternal mortality rates.

new_jobs.description:
At Early Warning, we’ve powered and protected the U.S. financial system for over thirty years with cutting\-edge solutions like Zelle®, Paze®, and so much more. As a trusted name in payments, we partner with thousands of institutions to increase access to financial services and protect transactions for hundreds of millions of consumers and small businesses.

  

Positions located in Scottsdale, San Francisco, Chicago, or New York follow a hybrid work model to allow for a more collaborative working environment.  



  

Candidates responding to this posting must independently possess the eligibility to work in the United States, for any employer, at the date of hire. This position is ineligible for employment Visa sponsorship.

**Overall Purpose**


The Sr. Fraud Program Manager is responsible for leading and maturing key components of Paze’s Fraud Program to safeguard customers and protect the integrity of the platform.

  

This role operates at a strategic and executional level — owning large, complex, cross\-functional fraud initiatives while influencing enterprise stakeholders across Product, Engineering, Risk, Compliance, Legal, and Operations.

  

The Sr. Lead partners closely with Fraud leadership to translate strategic objectives into scalable program structures, technical requirements, governance, and measurable outcomes. This position serves as the most senior individual contributor within the Fraud Risk Program function and may mentor other program managers.

 **Essential Functions**

* Lead the design, execution, and continuous improvement of major components of the Fraud Risk Program.
* Translate fraud strategy into executable roadmaps, epics, features, and technical requirements.
* Own delivery of large, complex, technology\-intensive fraud initiatives spanning multiple interrelated workstreams.
* Establish program governance frameworks, operating rhythms, KPIs, reporting mechanisms, and risk controls.
* Proactively monitor fraud performance metrics relative to targets; identify emerging risks and drive mitigation strategies.
* Lead program\-level risk identification, issue resolution, and change control across cross\-functional teams.
* Partner with Product, Engineering, Architecture, Security, Compliance, and Legal to align fraud risk capabilities with business strategy and roadmap priorities.
* Drive vendor oversight for fraud\-related third\-party solutions, ensuring performance, compliance, and risk standards are met.
* Develop and formalize fraud risk standards, policies, controls, and documentation aligned to regulatory requirements and industry best practices.
* Influence decision\-making at senior leadership levels through data\-driven recommendations and executive\-ready communication.
* Mentor and provide guidance to other Fraud Risk Program Managers to elevate program delivery practices.
* Support the company’s commitment to enterprise risk management and protection of systems and data integrity.

 **Minimum Qualifications**

* Bachelor’s degree in Business, Finance, Computer Science, Risk Management, or related field.
* Typically, 12\+ years of experience in banking, payments, fraud risk, or related risk management roles.
* 5\+ years of experience leading large, complex, cross\-functional fraud or payments programs.
* Demonstrated experience delivering technology\-intensive initiatives in partnership with engineering teams.
* Advanced knowledge of fraud risk management tools, controls, governance models, and industry best practices.
* Strong executive communication skills with the ability to influence senior stakeholders.
* Proven ability to operate autonomously in ambiguous, fast\-moving environments.
* Strong analytical and problem\-solving skills with a data\-driven mindset.
* PMP, Agile, Scrum, or equivalent program management certification (or equivalent experience).
* Background and drug screen.

 **Preferred Qualifications**

* Experience in digital banking, payments networks, or wallet ecosystems.
* Deep familiarity with fraud analytics, decision engines, or risk platforms.
* Experience scaling fraud programs in high\-growth environments.
* SAS, SQL, or comparable analytical coding experience.
* Demonstrated experience mentoring or leading other program managers.

 **Physical Requirements**


Working conditions consist of a normal office environment. Work is primarily sedentary and requires extensive use of a computer and involves sitting for periods of approximately four hours. Work may require occasional standing, walking, kneeling, and reaching. Must be able to lift 10 pounds occasionally and/or negligible amount of force frequently. Requires visual acuity and dexterity to view, prepare, and manipulate documents and office equipment including personal computers. Requires the ability to communicate with internal and/or external customers. Employee must be able to perform essential functions and physical requirements of position with or without reasonable accommodation.

=======================================================================


Under the direction of the Senior Property Operations Analyst, this position is responsible for ensuring rent increases are properly calculated, monitored and in accordance with Eden Housing’s rent increase policy as well as property, federal, local and state ordinances. This position oversees the rent increase process for a large portfolio of affordable units in northern and southern California. The Property Operations Rent Analyst will keep current with affordable housing rent changes under various housing programs to include (but not limited to) CTCAC, HUD, HOME, and HCD. They are responsible for maintaining and updating all non\-HUD Utility Allowance schedules in Yardi. Additionally, they will also be responsible for performing Accounts Receivable (AR) related tasks, such as (but not limited to) applying rent concessions to tenant ledgers, processing write\-offs for past tenant balances, and reviewing and monitoring accounts receivables reports and ledgers as assigned. This position will also assist the Senior Property Operations Analyst with various other tasks as assigned.


**ESSENTIAL DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES**




**Rent Increases**

* Optimize non\-subsidized rent revenue.
* Generate/analyze reports and rent rolls against maximum program allowable rent/income schedules.
* Maintain and update working tiered rent increase model data worksheet.
* Prepare calculations of proposed rent increases monthly.
* Assist with annual budgeting process by forecasting/estimating the amount of rent revenue to be achieved by site.
* Facilitate the annual rent increase process in accordance with company policy.
* Provide site staff rent increase information to be implemented appropriately and timely.
* Ensure that pertinent rent increase information is reviewed appropriately and timely by site staff and Compliance specialists.
* Process and resolve edits and comments from site staff and Compliance reviews prior to finalizing rent increase model workbook.
* Create and provide rent increase letters to site staff for distribution.
* Coordinate with Business Technology team to batch update lease charges in Yardi.
* Monitor if rent increases occur as planned and provide reports to property supervisors to hold site staff accountable.
* Verify that the rent limits are inputted correctly in Yardi as provided by Compliance.
* Ensure that the most up\-to\-date rent limits are used as the basis to calculate rent increases.
* Monitor tiered rent increase model data worksheet if any rent amounts are at or below the unit’s maximum allowable rent limit. If above:
	+ Perform appropriate lease charge and ledger adjustments.
	+ Create and provide rent decrease letters to site staff.
	+ Facilitate credit reimbursement refunds for overcharged rent, as necessary.

* Monitor and implement utility allowance schedules and verify that the utility allowances are inputted correctly in Yardi.
* Distribute program\-based letters to site staff and process HAP changes received from the Housing Authority.
* Manage Housing Authority mail correspondences received at the Central Office.
* Scan and distribute appropriately to site staff and other departments, as applicable.
* Process rent portion changes (tenant portion and subsidy/HAP) as informed by Housing Authority letters.
* Resolve and respond to Accounts Receivable help tickets as assigned, which include, but not limited to:
	+ Processing ledger corrections, rent concessions, write\-offs
	+ Reviewing and analyzing resident ledgers and receivables reports
	+ Assisting site staff with rent collection tasks and resolving issues
	+ Assisting site staff with move\-out and depositing accounting tasks and resolving issues

No supervisory responsibility.

Bachelor’s degree in business, Finance or Accounting from a four\-year college or university preferred; equivalent education and experience accepted.
